title: A look at the frameworks: Gin, Echo, Fiber and Beego

videos.script: Three lessons of boxoffice, and every line came from the standard library. Most Go services you will meet were not written that way. {{why}} Before Go 1.22 the standard router could not match a method or a wildcard. Routers and frameworks filled that gap, and they stayed. {{same}} So this lesson writes one small API five times. The standard library, then Gin, Echo, Fiber and Beego. Same routes, same rules, same six questions. {{gin}} Gin binds and validates from struct tags, and answers a wrong method with a 404. Echo turns every returned error into JSON. {{fiber}} Fiber is not net/http at all. It runs on fasthttp, and that has consequences. Beego brings a whole stack, down to an HTML error page. {{numbers}} Then the numbers. Lines of code, modules pulled in, and the size of the binary. One of those barely moves. The other two move a lot.
